title: EDTA: the calcium claw
topic: How EDTA grips one Ca²⁺ with six donor atoms, why ~1 min clears the smear layer, and why longer EDTA then NaOCl erodes dentine.

claims.claim: EDTA binds Ca²⁺ as the fully deprotonated EDTA⁴⁻
claims.source: Hülsmann M et al., Int Endod J 2003;36:810–30 (PMID 14641420); Martell AE & Smith RM, Critical Stability Constants (reference book, Plenum Press; not a journal article, not in PubMed)

claims.claim: Six donor atoms (4 carboxylate O⁻ + 2 amine N) grip one apatite Ca²⁺
claims.source: Hülsmann M et al., Int Endod J 2003;36:810–30 (PMID 14641420; review of EDTA chemistry); the 4 O⁻ + 2 N hexadentate donor set is standard coordination chemistry (Martell & Smith, reference book)

claims.claim: Binding order, arm motion, atom sizes and the apatite lattice are schematic; the real complex also binds water
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: constraint-relaxed EDTA geometry on a toy apatite lattice (CaEDTA crystal structure: Barnett BL, Uchtman VA, Inorg Chem 1979;18:2674–8, doi:10.1021/ic50200a007; verified via Crossref, not indexed in PubMed)
Hülsmann M et al., Int Endod J 2003;36:810–30 (PMID 14641420); Martell & Smith, Critical Stability Constants (reference book; log K CaEDTA²⁻ ≈ 10.7)
Mader CL, Baumgartner JC, Peters DD, J Endod 1984;10:477–83 (PMID 6593410; no PubMed abstract — the 1–2 µm figure is the standard attribution to this paper)

claims.claim: 17% EDTA (neutral pH) for ~1 min removes the smear layer and opens tubules (in vitro)
claims.source: Calt S, Serper A, J Endod 2002;28:17–9 (PMID 11806642); Serper A, Calt S, J Endod 2002;28:501–2 (PMID 12126374; neutral pH > pH 9); Crumpton BJ et al., J Endod 2005;31:536–8 (PMID 15980717; 1 mL 17% REDTA × 1 min, then NaOCl)

claims.claim: Least effective in the apical third
claims.source: Teixeira CS et al., Int Endod J 2005;38:285–90 (PMID 15876291)

claims.claim: 10 min EDTA, then NaOCl: peri- & intertubular erosion of dentine
claims.source: Calt S, Serper A, J Endod 2002;28:17–9 (PMID 11806642)

claims.claim: Erosion arises mainly when NaOCl follows EDTA; a final NaOCl after EDTA adds erosion
claims.source: Niu W et al., Int Endod J 2002;35:934–9 (PMID 12453023); Qian W et al., J Endod 2011;37:1437–41 (PMID 21924198)

claims.claim: NaOCl targets organic tissue, EDTA the mineral (Ca²⁺); never mix them
claims.source: Zehnder M, J Endod 2006;32:389–98 (PMID 16631834); Grawehr M et al., Int Endod J 2003;36:411–7 (PMID 12801288)

caption:
How does EDTA actually open dentinal tubules?
One EDTA⁴⁻ wraps a single Ca²⁺ with six donor atoms (4 O⁻ + 2 N) and carries it off as a 1:1 complex.
Scaled up: ~1 min of 17% EDTA removes the 1–2 µm smear layer in vitro, least reliably in the apical third.
Go longer and follow with NaOCl, and peri- and intertubular dentine erodes.
NaOCl for tissue, EDTA for mineral. Never mix them.
Refs: Calt & Serper 2002, J Endod; Mader 1984, J Endod; Teixeira 2005, Int Endod J; Niu 2002, Int Endod J; Qian 2011, J Endod; Grawehr 2003, Int Endod J
Animation is schematic (toy model, not to scale).
